prior_findings.note: cleanup() is correct on its own. It inspects the ref, runs `docker rmi <ref>` without -f and without sha256 only while the ref still resolves to the recorded id, and the default tag is now unique per run (clean-<tree7>-<8 hex>). Probes still address the image by id. Docker here uses the overlay2 store, so `{{.Id}}` equals the iidfile digest and the equality check holds. The destructive `rmi -f <id>` is gone. The edge cases hold once wiring is fixed: a ref re-tagged to another id fails the inspect match and is skipped; a failed build records no pair; a failed inspect is skipped, which leaks but never deletes. However, the N1 fix's recording step in run() crashes (COR-1), so cleanup never receives the (ref, id) pairs. With --remove-images, run() raises TypeError in the finally block and leaks the image it built. The only N1 test calls cleanup() in isolation. Side note: the random default tag is never printed. Runs without --remove-images (the Makefile target and the ps1 default) leave tags that the output never names.

--require-registry-match is wired into the CLI, the Makefile clean-checkout target, check_clean_checkout.ps1 (on by default, -AllowRegistryDrift opts out) and the gate test. The gate's formula len(IMAGES) + sum((1 if module else 0) + len(probes)) equals verdict's len(steps) + sum(len(step.probes)), because probe_commands emits [module] (if any) plus probes. The test passes neither --compose nor --tests. With rc 0 the last stdout line is exactly 'N/N steps ok'. The test also asserts len(IMAGES) >= 10 and no drift warning. The c1 unit test fails on fix1 (no build_parser). The gate cannot actually pass until COR-1 is fixed.

GIT_* is stripped for resolve_tree, export_tree's git archive, both _git_context calls and tests_env. After init, --absolute-git-dir must resolve to out/.git. Run against the fix1 snapshot, the new test fails (`add -A` exit 128 after GIT_DIR turned the other repo bare); it passes now. checkpoint.ps1 overrides only GIT_INDEX_FILE and write-tree stores objects in the normal object store, so the stripping cannot hide checkpoint trees.

main() resolves the tree-ish once with `rev-parse --verify --quiet <tree>^{tree}`, with a GIT_*-free env. It passes the full id to resolve_out (default out path), default_tag and run(), and run() writes that id into the export marker. The ps1 forwards the raw -Tree, which main() then resolves. The test fails on fix1 (no resolve_tree). Gap: no test covers main()'s wiring, so a main() that went back to args.tree would still pass.

The untracked services/b/helper.py is reported under the old global roots. The test passes on the current checker. Non-vacuous.

findings.problem: Fix2 renamed the list of built (ref, id) pairs from `built_ids` to `built` (line 232), but the build loop already used `built` for the bool returned by `_run`. Line 238 rebinds `built` to True or False. After the first successful build, line 241 `built.append((ref, image_id))` raises AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'append'. With --remove-images, the finally block then calls `cleanup(built)` with a bool (line 257) and raises TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable.
findings.failure_scenario: Every real proof crashes with a traceback and exit 1 right after `[ok] build orchestrator-service`, before any probe runs or any other image is built. That covers `make clean-checkout TREE=...`, check_clean_checkout.ps1, the realinfra gate test test_mvp_008_tree_builds_and_probes_from_clean_checkout and the W0 barrier run `clean_checkout.py --tree <barrier tree> --compose`. With --remove-images (which the gate test always passes), cleanup also crashes, so the built image is leaked. Even a run where every build fails (the negative-control shape) ends in TypeError when --remove-images is set. MVP-008 cannot close on this tool, and the C1 gate cannot pass.
findings.fix: Use a separate name for the build result: `ok = _run(f"build {step.image.name}", ...)` and `image_id = ... if ok and iid.is_file() else ""`. Add a unit test that drives run(), or main() so that N2's wiring is also covered, with a fake subprocess layer: a fake `docker build` writes the --iidfile, and probes return rc 0. Assert rc 0 and the last line 'N/N steps ok' with N = images + modules + probes. With remove_images=True, assert that cleanup receives the (ref, id) pairs and issues `docker rmi <ref>` only.

prior_findings.note: The cleanup() design is right: it untags by reference, without -f, and only while the ref still points at the recorded id. But run() never reaches it, because the variable `built` is shadowed. The fix is unreachable and is untested.

--require-registry-match is wired into the Makefile and the PowerShell wrapper, which defaults to strict and has an explicit -AllowRegistryDrift opt-out. The realinfra gate test pins the exact step count from len(IMAGES) and asserts len(IMAGES) >= 10. A shrunken registry cannot pass it.

git_env() strips GIT_* from resolve_tree, git archive and _git_context. tests_env also drops GIT_*, and _git_context asserts the absolute git dir is out/.git. The c2 test covers GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE.
resolve_tree() resolves any tree-ish to a full tree id, and default_tag yields a valid docker tag of the form clean-<7>-<8hex>.
The r1 test now places helper.py at services/b/helper.py, so it is no longer vacuous.

findings.problem: In run(), the list `built: list[tuple[str, str]]` (line 232) is rebound inside the step loop by `built = _run(...)`, which returns a bool. Line 241 then calls `built.append((ref, image_id))` on that bool, and the finally block calls `cleanup(built)` with the same variable.
findings.failure_scenario: The first successful `docker build` sets built=True and image_id is non-empty. `built.append` then raises AttributeError ('bool' object has no attribute 'append'). The run aborts mid-way, so no later image is built or probed and no verdict is printed. If --remove-images is set, cleanup(True) in the finally block raises TypeError from dict.fromkeys(True), which masks the original error. The N1 untag-by-ref fix therefore never executes. Images already built are left behind with their random tags, which is the operator-safety problem N1 was meant to close. The offline unit tests call cleanup() directly and never exercise run(), so they stay green. The real-infra gate test would fail, but only when a lane runs it. fix1 used a separate `built_ids` list and did not have this bug, so it is a fix2 regression.
findings.fix: Rename the bool, e.g. `ok = _run(...)` and `image_id = ... if ok and iid.is_file() else ""`, and keep `built` as the list. Add an offline test that drives run() with subprocess.run, export_tree and load_registry monkeypatched (a fake docker that writes the iidfile). It should assert that cleanup receives the (ref, id) pairs and that `docker rmi <ref>` is issued without -f.

Confirmed at clean_checkout.py lines 232-257. `built` is declared as a list at line 232, then rebound to a bool at line 238 by `_run`, which returns `ok`. On a successful build, line 241 calls `built.append(...)` on a bool and raises AttributeError. On a failed build, `built` is False and the later `cleanup(built)` fails the same way. The run aborts, and `cleanup(True)` in the finally block raises TypeError from `dict.fromkeys(True)` when --remove-images is set. That masks the original error, and no cleanup happens.
